model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms for the Mistralv0.2-Base model, both before and after fine-tuning on six distinct medical specialties: Cardio (Cardiology), Gastro (Gastroenterology), Infect (Infectious Disease), Neuro (Neurology), Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., lower uncertainty) in predicting those terms. The horizontal axis groups bars by specialty, with each group containing seven bars: one light blue bar representing the base model’s performance, followed by six bars in varying shades of orange and brown corresponding to the fine-tuned model’s performance on each specialty. In each group, the fine-tuned bars consistently show lower (better) negative log probabilities than the base model bar, indicating improved term prediction after fine-tuning. The bars within each specialty group are sorted in descending order of performance (lowest negative log probability first), with the best-performing fine-tuned model for that specialty shown first. The legend at the top clarifies the color coding for each specialty, and the chart title “Fine-tuned on:” reinforces that the colored bars reflect performance after fine-tuning on the respective domain. Notably, for most specialties, the fine-tuned model achieves negative log probabilities between approximately -23 and -26, while the base model typically performs worse, often near -27. The chart visually emphasizes that domain-specific fine-tuning significantly improves the model’s ability to predict terminology relevant to each medical specialty.
